data.name: Help_HeaderSubtitle
data.value: Touch Mapping, EDID Collisions and Range Extenders

data.name: Help_S1_Body
data.value:
Windows cannot permanently assign a touch digitizer to a specific monitor when several identical monitors are attached. On this installation both DM7000 units report the same EDID, including the same serial number, and both PM1715 digitizers provide no physical location path. The operating system therefore has no criterion at all for telling left from right — after a restart or a DisplayPort event, the mappings can end up swapped.
The agent supplies the missing criterion: a mapping learned once, anchored to the digitizer's USB port and the monitor's graphics connector — both physical properties that survive a restart.

data.name: Help_S2_Step1Text
data.value: Open the main window (double-click the tray icon).

data.name: Help_S2_Step2Text
data.value: In the monitor list, select the screen to be learned. The list shows connector and position, because both panels carry the same name.

data.name: Help_S2_Step3Text
data.value: Press "Learn Screen (Touch)". A full-screen window appears on the selected screen.

data.name: Help_S2_Step4Text
data.value: Touch that screen. The agent identifies which digitizer sent the touch from the raw input signal and permanently links it to that monitor's port.

data.name: Help_S2_Closing
data.value: One pass per screen is then enough. The agent restores the mapping by itself after every restart and every DisplayPort event.

data.name: Help_S3_Body1
data.value: The touch mapping itself does not need this — it uses the PnP device path, which is unique regardless. An EDID collision does, however, disrupt every

data.name: Help_S3_Body2
data.value: piece of software on the machine that identifies screens by their serial number.

data.name: Help_S3_Body3
data.value: In the EDID manager, the "EDID Status" column shows the finding. "EDID Collision" means: another monitor reports exactly the same identity. "Auto-Resolve Collisions" then assigns each device a unique serial number and installs it as a Windows EDID override.

data.name: Help_S3_Body4
data.value: When two monitors share only the numeric serial number but differ in their text descriptor, the agent deliberately does not intervene — they are distinguishable. The value 0x01010101 is a common placeholder for "serial number not programmed"; rewriting such panels would achieve nothing and would alter firmware data without need.

data.name: Help_S4_Body1
data.value: Extenders frequently do not pass DDC through. Two symptoms:

data.name: Help_S4_TextA
data.value: The transmitter unit responds with a block burned into the extender by its manufacturer, instead of the panel's EDID. If both extenders are identical, the graphics driver sees the same fingerprint twice — this is the cause of the collision on this installation.

data.name: Help_S4_TextB
data.value: The port shows a picture but reports no EDID. The manager shows "Extender / No-EDID".

data.name: Help_S4_SolutionSteps
data.value: 1. Install an EDID template from the panel manufacturer (.bin, .hex or .inf). The supplied template DM7000_Native.bin contains the EDID actually measured from the DM7000. 2. If no template is available: "Generate Synthetic EDID from Current Signal". The agent builds a standards-compliant block from it.

data.name: Help_S4_SyntheticText
data.value: It is a stopgap. It describes the mode Windows is currently driving, but contains no manufacturer-specific timings and no colour values measured at the panel. Colour reproduction and DPI scaling remain approximations, and further modes of the panel stay invisible to Windows. Where a genuine EDID or a manufacturer driver exists, either is the better source.

data.name: Help_S4_HandshakeText
data.value: If the screens stay black ("no signal") after a restart and only work after a power cycle at the extender, the hot-plug-detect chain is interrupted during boot. An EDID override only helps to a limited extent here — active DP-to-HDMI adapters, an EDID emulator right at the graphics output, or a power supply where the extenders come up before the server can remedy this.

data.name: Help_S5_Heading
data.value: 5. Important: The Agent Must Keep Running

data.name: Help_S5_Body1
data.value: The service decides which mapping needs to be restored, but cannot carry that out itself: it runs in Session 0 and can neither see the desktop nor start tabcal.exe. Only the tray agent in the user session can do that.

data.name: Help_S5_Body2
data.value: If the agent is closed via "Exit", the mapping will not be restored after the next restart. Closing via the "X" does not exit it — it keeps running in the notification area.

data.name: Help_S6_Body1
data.value: "Export Diagnostics Log" in the tray menu writes the service's and client's logs, plus a snapshot of the detected hardware, to a file.

data.name: Tray_ExitWarning
data.value:
IMPORTANT NOTICE: Windows has no built-in way to permanently map touch digitizers to identical monitors.
If you exit this agent, the system can no longer maintain the mapping across restarts or DisplayPort events (touch input will land on the wrong screen).
Do you really want to exit the agent?
